# AES Control FSM Behavioral Specification

## 1. Purpose

This module is the main control block for the AES unit. It determines when a block operation may start, when it is complete, when input and output data can be accepted or read, and when key, IV, and data registers must be cleared. It also manages pseudo-random generator reseeding and reports the operational status of the AES unit.

This specification describes only the local behavior of this control module.

---

## 2. Reset and Initial State

- After reset, the module shall be in its normal idle state.
- In idle state, it shall not issue any operation requests, shall not write any registers, and shall not assert an alert.
- All status outputs shall be in their cleared state after reset.

---

## 3. Starting a Block Operation

### 3.1 General Start Conditions

The module shall only allow a block operation to start when:

- The configured cipher mode is valid and not “none”.
- There is no storage error in the control configuration.
- No fatal alert indication is active.
- The configured cipher operation is a valid forward or inverse operation.

### 3.2 Automatic Mode

In automatic mode, the module shall start encryption or decryption automatically when all of the following are true:

- The initial key is usable.
- A complete input data block is available.
- The mode-specific IV/counter requirements are satisfied.
- No clear or reseed operation is pending.

The mode-specific requirements are:

- ECB: no IV is required.
- CBC, CFB, OFB: the IV must be usable.
- CTR: the IV must be usable and the counter must be ready.

The module shall consider the initial key usable when all initial key registers have been written since the last control-register update, or when they were already complete and have not been invalidated. A partially written key shall not be used.

The module shall consider the IV usable when all IV registers have been written since the last IV update, or when none of them have been written since the last completed use. A partially written IV shall not be used.

The module shall consider an input data block complete when each input data register has been written at least once since the previous block was consumed or cleared. The order of writes shall not matter.

### 3.3 Manual Mode

In manual mode, the module shall start a block operation only when a start command is asserted. Manual mode shall have priority over automatic start conditions.

In manual mode, the module shall not require the initial key, IV, or input data readiness conditions to be satisfied. It shall start using the current contents of the relevant registers. The configuration must still be valid and no fatal alert indication may be active.

### 3.4 Actions When a Start Is Accepted

When the module accepts a start, it shall:

- Signal the start of an encryption or decryption operation.
- Load the current initial key, IV, and input data into the processing datapath as required by the selected mode.
- Preserve the previous input data block when needed for CBC decryption, CFB, OFB, or CTR operation.
- Trigger the appropriate mode-specific IV and counter behavior.
- Cause the input data block to be considered consumed so that a new input block may be accepted afterward.

### 3.5 Decryption Start-Key Generation

If the selected operation is ECB or CBC decryption and the initial key has been newly provided, the module shall first arrange for the decryption start key to be generated before processing any data block.

During this start-key generation:

- No input data block shall be consumed.
- No IV shall be consumed.
- No output data shall be written.
- A start command in manual mode shall remain pending and shall be honored once the start-key generation completes.

Once start-key generation is complete, the module shall return to idle and then start the actual data block operation using the same key, IV, and input data.

---

## 4. Completing a Block Operation

The module shall only complete a block operation when the processing datapath indicates that a result is available and the completion is allowed.

In automatic mode, completion shall be allowed only when:

- The previous output data block, if any, has been fully read, or
- No previous output data block is still pending.

If a new output result is ready but the previous output has not been fully read, the module shall not overwrite it. It shall stall the completion of the new result and assert the stall status.

In manual mode, the module shall allow completion even if the previous output has not been read. Overwriting an unread output block shall cause the output-lost status to be set.

### 4.1 Output Data Acceptance

When a block result is accepted, the module shall:

- Write the output data into the output data registers.
- Assert the output-valid status.
- Update the IV registers according to the selected mode.
- Decrement the block count used for reseeding.
- Return to idle.

The module shall not write output data if a fault condition on a selector or safety-related encoding is detected at completion time.

### 4.2 Output-Valid and Output-Read Tracking

The output-valid status shall be asserted when a new output block is written.

It shall remain asserted until every output data register has been read at least once. The order of reads shall not matter.

If all output registers are read in the same cycle in which a new output block is written, the output-valid status shall remain asserted.

### 4.3 Output-Lost Tracking

The output-lost status shall be set whenever a new output block is written while the previous output block is still valid and has not been fully read.

Once set, it shall remain set until the control configuration is updated, starting a new message context.

---

## 5. Configuration and Register Update Behavior

### 5.1 Control-Register Updates

The module shall allow a control-register update only when it is idle and not starting, clearing, or reseeding in the same cycle.

A control-register update shall invalidate the current initial-key, IV, input-data, and output-data status tracking. This ensures that a new message requires fresh key, IV, and data programming.

A control-register update shall be ignored when a storage error is present. A storage error is unrecoverable and requires a reset.

### 5.2 Initial Key Register Updates

When key sideload is disabled, the module shall accept software writes to the initial key registers only while idle and not starting, clearing, or reseeding.

When key sideload is enabled:

- Software writes to the initial key registers shall be ignored.
- The initial key shall be taken from the sideload key source.
- The module shall only start if the sideload key is valid.
- The sideload key shall be captured after a control-register update so that key changes can be detected.

### 5.3 IV Register Updates

Software writes to the IV registers shall be accepted only while the module is idle and not starting, clearing, or reseeding in the same cycle.

When operating in CBC, CFB, OFB, or CTR mode, the module shall update the IV registers automatically according to the mode. Software shall not be allowed to partially update an IV that is about to be used.

### 5.4 Input Data Register Updates

The module shall expose an input-ready status:

- It shall be asserted when no complete input data block is pending.
- It shall be deasserted once all four input data registers have been written and a complete block is pending.
- It shall be reasserted when that block is consumed by the datapath or when the input-status tracking is cleared.

### 5.5 Output Data Register Updates

The module shall expose an output-valid status as described above.

Reading all output data registers shall clear the output-valid status unless new output data is written in the same cycle.

Clearing output data registers with pseudo-random data shall not assert output-valid.

---

## 6. Clearing Operations

### 6.1 Clear Commands

The module supports commands to clear key, IV, and input-data registers, and to clear output-data registers. These commands may be issued together.

### 6.2 Clear Sequence

Before performing a clear, the module shall request fresh pseudo-random data and wait until it is available.

After fresh pseudo-random data is available:

- If the key/IV/data-in clear command is active, the module shall clear:
  - all initial key registers,
  - all IV registers,
  - all input data registers,
  - the previous input data storage,
  - and coordinate clearing of internal key registers inside the processing datapath.
- If the data-out clear command is active, the module shall clear all output data registers, and coordinate clearing of internal state as needed.

The module shall clear the corresponding command bits only after the relevant portion of the clear operation has completed.

Clearing shall not produce an output-valid indication.

If a fault on a selector or safety-related encoding is detected during the output-clearing phase, the module shall not release or write output data.

---

## 7. PRNG Reseeding

### 7.1 Reseed Requests

The module shall perform a pseudo-random generator reseed when:

- A software reseed command is asserted, or
- A new key has been provided and the key-touch-forces-reseed option is enabled.

A reseed operation shall have priority over clear commands and block start commands.

### 7.2 Reseed Behavior

During a reseed operation, the module shall:

- Issue a reseed request and wait until the reseed is acknowledged.
- If masking is enabled, also wait for the processing datapath to reseed its internal masking randomness.
- Clear the reseed command after completion.
- Return to idle.

The module shall not assert the idle status while a reseed is in progress.

### 7.3 Block-Based Reseeding

The module shall maintain a block count for reseeding purposes.

The block count shall be:

- Reset when a new message is configured via a control-register update.
- Decremented after each completed block.
- Used to request a masking reseed when the configured reseed interval has been reached.

If masking is disabled, block-based reseeding is not required.

---

## 8. Fault Handling and Terminal Error State

### 8.1 Fault Conditions

The module shall enter its terminal error state when any of the following is detected:

- An invalid cipher operation encoding.
- An invalid sparse encoding on a safety-related control input.
- An invalid mux selector indication.
- A life-cycle escalation request is active.

A fatal alert indication shall prevent the module from starting or completing block operations. If configured to do so, the module shall also force status and trigger outputs to their cleared values while a fatal alert indication is present.

### 8.2 Behavior in Terminal Error State

In the terminal error state, the module shall:

- Assert its alert output continuously.
- Not start or complete any block operation.
- Not write any key, IV, input, or output registers.
- Not issue any new operation or reseed requests.
- Ignore start, clear, and reseed commands.
- Remain in this state until reset.

---

## 9. Mode-Specific Chaining Behavior

The module shall implement the following IV and data-chaining behavior:

- CBC encryption: after a block completes, the IV registers shall be updated with the ciphertext output block.
- CBC decryption: after a block completes, the IV registers shall be updated with the previous input data block.
- CFB: after a block completes, the IV registers shall be updated with the ciphertext output block.
- OFB: after a block completes, the IV registers shall be updated with the raw cipher output before it is combined with the previous input data.
- CTR: the IV/counter registers shall be updated by the counter during the block operation, and the module shall command one counter increment per block.

In CBC, CFB, OFB, and CTR modes, the module shall preserve the current input data block for as long as it is needed for chaining.

---

## 10. Summary of Status Behavior

The module shall provide the following status behavior:

- Idle: asserted when the module is ready to accept configuration and no operation, clear, or reseed is active or starting.
- Stall: asserted when a completed output cannot be accepted because the previous output has not been read. Manual mode shall not assert stall.
- Input ready: asserted when a new input data block can be accepted.
- Output valid: asserted when new output data is available.
- Output lost: asserted when output data has been overwritten before being read, and remains set until the next control-register update.
